expected_evidence: geological: a synchronous ~12,900 cal BP 'Younger Dryas boundary' layer across multiple continents containing platinum anomalies, iridium enrichment, nanodiamonds, magnetic/glass spherules, and elevated soot/charcoal indicating continent-scale biomass burning
geological: black mat / dark organic-rich layer marking abrupt ecological transition at YD onset
astronomical: orbital-dynamics reconstructions showing the Taurid meteor stream/complex had a much denser, fragmenting parent body ~12,900 years ago capable of producing an airburst/impact cluster
astronomical: identification of candidate impact structures or airburst signatures (e.g., proposed craters, disturbed strata) aligned with Taurid orbital nodes

material (archaeological): abrupt discontinuities in Clovis-era and other Upper Paleolithic occupation layers, ash lenses, or fire-affected sediments at multiple sites correlating with the boundary layer
genetic: megafaunal population bottleneck/extinction signatures dated to the YD onset consistent with a sudden environmental shock
geological: sedimentary/ice-core proxies (e.g., ammonium, nitrate spikes) suggesting biomass-burning-driven atmospheric loading and cooling ('impact winter')
oral_tradition: cross-cultural flood/fire/sky-catastrophe myths sometimes invoked as folk memory (weak, highly speculative)
iconographic: Paleolithic cave/rock art motifs (e.g., Göbekli Tepe pillar carvings) proposed by some researchers as symbolic records of a cometary event (contested, model-prior only)
response.rationale: Using the 'younger-dryas' row (interval matches YD onset, ~10,950 BCE / 12,900 cal BP) as the operative period, the strongest expected signals are geological (0.65) and astronomical/orbital-dynamics (0.7), since a genuine multi-continental impact-winter event should leave a synchronous sedimentary boundary layer (platinum, iridium, nanodiamonds, soot/charcoal, black mat) and should be reconstructible from Taurid stream orbital modeling. These evidence types are indeed the ones actually invoked in the real-world Younger Dryas Impact Hypothesis (YDIH) literature, and comparable boundary-layer data have been reported at numerous sites worldwide — so the type of evidence the hypothesis predicts is not merely hypothetical; searches for it have been conducted and some candidate signals have been published, though their interpretation remains scientifically contested (many researchers attribute the same proxies to non-impact causes like wildfire or diagenesis). Material/archaeological (0.35) and genetic (0.3) evidence for Upper Paleolithic populations is much sparser due to poor preservation, low population density, and the absence of written or dense material records this far back, and this scarcity is largely a preservation/sampling artifact rather than proof the event didn't happen. Textual (0.0) and linguistic (0.05) evidence are essentially impossible this early (pre-writing, minimal linguistic reconstruction depth), so their absence carries no evidentiary weight against the hypothesis. Oral tradition (0.1) and iconographic (0.1) claims (e.g., proposed comet imagery at Göbekli Tepe) are frequently cited by impact-hypothesis proponents but are extremely low-confidence, speculative, and reliant on my own uncorroborated training-derived knowledge (model-prior only), not verified evidence in this pipeline. Because corroboration requires convergent multi-continental geological and astronomical signals — both of which have moderate-to-good preservation/detectability — a low overall evidence yield should not be read as strong disconfirmation; rather, the mixed and contested nature of published findings reflects genuine scientific disagreement layered on top of moderate-but-imperfect detectability. I set the combined detectability_adjustment at 0.5, blending the higher geological/astronomical plausibility with the much weaker material/genetic/textual/oral channels, and explicitly flag that any astronomical/orbital-mechanics claims about the Taurid complex's ancient structure, and any iconographic/oral-tradition claims, rely on model-prior knowledge rather than verified sourced evidence in this task.
